definitions.explanation: The lower part of the leg below the ankle.
The entire lower limb from hip to foot.

examples.japanese: {靴|くつ}が{小|ちい}さくて、{足|あし}が{痛|いた}いです。
examples.english: My shoes are small, so my feet hurt.

examples.japanese: {足|あし}のサイズは{何|なん}センチですか。
examples.english: What size are your feet (in centimeters)?

examples.japanese: {一日中|いちにちじゅう}{歩|ある}いたので、{足|あし}がとても{疲|つか}れました。{今日|きょう}はもう{歩|ある}きたくないです。
examples.english: I walked all day, so my feet are very tired. I don't want to walk anymore today.

examples.notes: {足|あし}が{速|はや}い = fast runner

examples.japanese: {足|あし}を{組|く}まないでください。
{足|あし}が{遅|おそ}いので、みんなについていけません。
examples.english: I'm slow, so I can't keep up with everyone.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{足|あし}が{長|なが}くて、モデルのようです。{走|はし}るのも{速|はや}いし、スポーツも{上手|じょうず}です。
examples.english: He has long legs, like a model. He runs fast too and is good at sports.

notes:
{足|あし} covers both "foot" and "leg" in Japanese—there's no separate word for each.

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {足|あし}が{速|はや}い: to be fast (at running)
- {足|あし}が{遅|おそ}い: to be slow
- {足|あし}を{組|く}む: to cross one's legs
- {足|あし}が{棒|ぼう}になる: legs become like sticks (exhausted from walking)
- {足|あし}を{引|ひ}っ{張|ぱ}る: to hold someone back (idiom)

COMPOUNDS:
- {足首|あしくび}: ankle
- {足跡|あしあと}: footprint
- {素足|すあし}: bare feet
- {足音|あしおと}: footsteps

BODY PART PARALLEL:
Just as {足|あし} means both foot and leg, {手|て} means both hand and arm.
